html:
Anton de Kom was a Surinamese writer and activist, author of We Slaves of Suriname (1934), the first history of the colony told from the side of the enslaved and their descendants.

Born in Paramaribo, the son of a man born into slavery, he moved to the Netherlands and joined anti-colonial circles. In 1933 he returned home, drew crowds of workers of all groups, and was arrested and deported. His book, censored at first, attacked Dutch rule and celebrated the Maroons.

In the Second World War he joined the Dutch resistance against Germany. He was arrested in 1944 and died in a concentration camp in 1945. After independence he was honoured as a national hero of Suriname, and the university of Paramaribo bears his name.
